Security and privacy

VIKI Agent serves its window from a local loopback address. By default, it starts the installed Claude Code CLI on the sign-in Claude Code is set up with, such as your Claude plan or an API key. An explicit custom model connection uses VIKI's local gateway to send inference to the endpoint you choose.

Important

Claude Code can send prompts, tool results and other conversation data to its provider as part of a chat. Review what you send and which files you let its tools read.

VIKI Agent is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Settings › Diagnostics and About and the Your data and privacy topic in Help list where your data goes. The sections below give the details.

01Claude sign-in and plan usage

Sign in opens Claude Code's own claude auth login in a terminal window. The sign-in completes in Claude Code's flow. VIKI does not open Claude Code's credential file and keeps no copy of your sign-in. Its billing check reads Claude Code's settings files and keeps only the names of settings that would bill another account.

Chats VIKI starts on its own, routines and Bot threads run Claude Code on your sign-in the same way a chat you start does, so they count against your plan or bill the account your Claude Code uses. Anthropic's legal and compliance page says the advertised usage limits for Pro, Max and Ultra plans "assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK". Anthropic sets how a Claude plan may be used with other applications and can change it; an API key, a cloud provider or your own model connection is billed by usage instead of drawing on plan limits.

To keep chats on your Claude subscription, turn off Let Claude Code use its other sign-in methods in Settings › Chat: a chat then does not start when Claude Code is set up to bill another account. See Configuration.

02Custom model connections

Under Settings › Providers › Chat models, add a Magpie model or routing group, or configure an endpoint under Advanced — Direct connections. Magpie holds its providers' API keys. For a Magpie model, VIKI saves the model choice and any Gateway access key you enter; for a direct connection, VIKI saves the endpoint and its API key.

  • Storage
    saved connection details and keys are encrypted in VIKI's app storage. Settings and diagnostics exports omit them.
  • Other apps
    VIKI's connection form uses the key you enter. VIKI does not open other apps' credential files; Magpie's own behavior is described below.
  • Removing a connection
    removes its saved details and key. Conversation history remains with Claude Code. Removing the default returns new chats to Claude Code's own sign-in. Removing a connection also prevents its chats from continuing after their process closes.
  • Updating a key
    the connection stays the same connection, so chats and a default model that use it keep using it. Open chats keep using their captured key until you close and reopen them.
  • Portable exports and imports
    exports omit keys and a default model that names a saved connection. Imports reject such a default, because the connection belongs to this computer.

For a custom connection, Claude Code receives a temporary credential for VIKI's loopback gateway. Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway.

  • Access
    the gateway accepts only that Claude Code process's credential and refuses browser-origin requests. The window's launch token grants no access to it.
  • Endpoint key
    the server keeps it and sends requests to the configured endpoint over HTTPS, or HTTP for a server on this computer.
  • TLS and redirects
    the gateway verifies TLS and refuses redirects.
  • Tools
    the gateway translates model requests and replies. Claude Code executes the tools under its own permissions and hooks.
  • Connection failures
    unsupported requests and incomplete replies fail at the selected connection. A gateway such as Magpie can route or retry requests behind that connection.
  • Local inference
    requires a local model server that you run.
  • After a failure
    a failed or interrupted inference blocks further upstream requests from that process, including Claude Code's own retries. Close and reopen the chat after fixing the connection to try again.

Listing connections and saving one make no inference request.

  • List models
    queries the endpoint's model list.
  • Test connection
    sends a fixed short prompt, which the provider may charge for. It sends no conversation or vault content.
  • Default model
    the chosen default applies to new chats, including chats started by automation. Changing the default does not retarget saved chats.
  • Profiles, Bots and inbox suggestions
    these use native Claude models, except that a Bot's profile may pin a saved connection for its main chat, task threads and Bot-thread turns. Its routine runs use the native default, and a plain Agents › Profiles chat on it is refused. The endpoint can receive the whole conversation, including prompts, attachments and earlier replies, plus the Bot's profile instructions, memory rule and Bot rules, loaded Bot memory, the instruction files and skills Claude Code loads, tool results, and code or files a chat reads.
  • Existing transcripts
    an existing transcript without a saved VIKI model choice requires an explicit choice before using a connection default.
  • Model review
    if the chosen model has changed or cannot be confirmed when a chat opens, a notice asks you to review the model. Your draft stays unsent until you select Reopen chat, review the model and select Send again.

Set up models and connections in Settings › Providers › Chat models.

03The viki-agent command in chats

A chat you opened in the VIKI Agent window can run its own viki-agent command to read and change settings, routines and Bots.

  • Who gets a key
    VIKI Agent issues a new credential to each ordinary chat's Claude process, including on resume, and revokes it when that process closes. A profile chat, a Bot's chat or task thread, and a routine run never get one, reopened or not. A chat VIKI starts and runs on its own — a Decision mission, an inbox suggestion run, a messaging bridge's conversation — gets none of its own either, but reopening its transcript from the window gets it a key like any chat you opened there.
  • The three variables
    VIKI_AGENT_URL, VIKI_AGENT_KEY and VIKI_AGENT_CLI, set only in that process's own environment. Nothing logs the key, even by accident.
  • Loopback only
    the command reaches only 127.0.0.1, on this computer.
  • Access
    the surface accepts only that chat process's own key, refuses a request carrying an Origin, and accepts no window token.
  • Credentials stay out of reach
    a request to read or change a credential setting is refused, and the surface leaves it out of every reply.
  • Apply
    changing how the window looks, its layout, the code editor, a Bot's color or icon, or read-aloud speed and voice takes effect at once. Every other setting, and turning on a routine, waits for your Apply in the window; that Apply route accepts only the window's own token, never a chat's. Reject, or leaving it, changes nothing.
  • If it doesn't answer
    a command that times out exits with code 4, and its JSON error code no_reply means the request may already have gone through; its own guidance checks status before running anything again rather than assuming nothing happened.
  • Limit
    these levels, and the Apply route above, guard only this one command's surface. Claude Code's own permission rules still decide what every other command in that chat may do.

04Magpie routing and management

Open Magpie starts the bundled Magpie process and its dashboard. Magpie manages its own providers, routing groups, plugins and agent configuration. It can change agent settings and run plugins and MCP servers. Those actions use Magpie's controls and your account's system access; VIKI's chat permission cards govern Claude Code's chat tool requests.

VIKI starts its bundled Magpie with Magpie's subscription accounts setting off (MAGPIE_NO_ACCOUNTS=1). Magpie's documentation says this keeps it from reading agents' sign-ins, such as Claude Code's and Codex's files and the Keychain, and its source says it then serves no subscription account. API-key providers and local models work. Magpie uses no subscription plan, so choose an API-key or local model for the connection. A provider you add that signs in through another tool, such as Google Vertex AI through gcloud, uses that tool's credentials.

Magpie keeps provider keys, usage records and caches in its own files, and can record history. Enter those provider keys in Magpie. VIKI's optional Gateway access key is only for authenticating to Magpie's gateway, not to its providers. VIKI does not copy Magpie's credentials into its saved connections. VIKI settings exports and settings reset do not include Magpie's data. Review Magpie's storage and privacy settings before adding provider keys or enabling request recording. VIKI stops its bundled Magpie process when it begins to quit. On macOS and Linux, after a crash or a forced kill, a Magpie left running is stopped the next time VIKI starts, or at a later start or Magpie use if it cannot be identified then; on Windows it ends with VIKI. Magpie exports use the system Save As dialog and your account's file permissions, separately from VIKI's note-save controls.

The dashboard has a separate access key. The desktop app shows it in an isolated view with its own browser session; it receives no VIKI launch token and cannot request VIKI's origin. Its VIKI appearance uses local fonts and display settings; its credentials and data stay separate. In a browser window, the dashboard opens in your system browser. Keep its access key private.

Magpie's routing groups may retry requests or switch providers and models before returning an answer. Changing a group can change where an open chat sends inference. VIKI's failed-connection notice applies when Magpie returns a failure; it does not describe every attempt Magpie makes upstream.

The bundled process disables Magpie's user-count telemetry and starts with self-updates off. Keep its self-updates off and use a VIKI installer to update the bundled version. VIKI checks the pinned executable before starting it; a modified executable is refused. Magpie can fetch external model catalogs and icons, and its partner links and services have their own privacy behavior. Its routing and retention controls are in the Magpie dashboard. Review the Magpie documentation for those features.

05Decide what to trust

Claude Code runs with your account's file and process rights. It loads its usual instructions, skills, hooks and permission rules.

  • Permission cards
    VIKI Agent shows Allow once and Deny when the CLI asks it to decide a tool call. A call already permitted or denied by the CLI's mode, rules or hooks may produce no app card.
  • Permission modes
    an ordinary chat starts in its selected permission mode. The mode chip in its header switches the running chat to Manual, Accept edits, Auto or Plan, never to bypassPermissions or dontAsk. A profile chat keeps its profile's mode.
  • Checks and previews
    in a trusted code folder, these run with your account's rights. Inspect commands and changes before running them.
  • MCP server switches
    turning a server on or off in the chat bar's MCP servers dialog asks Claude Code to save that choice in its own settings for the chat's folder. The app itself writes nothing there.

Warning

A tool permission is separate from VIKI Agent's own note Save and note actions. Neither is a sandbox for a code folder or content returned by a tool.

Folders chats can also work in

A tick in Settings gives every new ordinary chat that folder too. Only a trusted code folder can be ticked.

  • Access
    Claude Code reads the folder without asking. It edits it following the chat's own permission mode.
  • What it loads
    Claude Code loads that folder's own skills, commands and agents, and its plugin choices. A plugin those choices enable may bring its own hooks and MCP servers. The folder's CLAUDE.md loads only when your own Claude Code setting turns that on, and its AGENTS.md does not load (Whose instructions a chat reads).
  • Chats left out
    profile chats, routines, Bots, the suggestion run and Workbench chats gain no folder this way. A Bot's own code folder works differently (Bot code copies).
  • Timing
    a tick or untick applies to chats started afterwards. A chat already open keeps the folders it started with until its process stops.

The folder picker returns the chosen paths only. Registering one as a vault or a code folder runs the same checks as a typed path.

Bot code copies

A Bot you gave a code folder works in a copy of it: a Git worktree of that repository (see Code copies for a Bot). A copy is not a sandbox.

  • What a chat gets
    the copy as one added folder, beside its vault. A grant adds no model, note-write or permission authority. Claude Code's own permissions decide what a Bot reads, edits and runs there.
  • Shared Git data
    a copy shares its repository's refs, config and objects with the folder and its other worktrees. A Bot can create, move and delete branches and tags, and what it does there can affect other worktrees.
  • Git run by Claude Code
    Git commands Claude Code runs in the copy are tool calls under its own permissions, and they run the folder's hooks as in any folder.
  • What the copy loads
    for that chat, and for later turns and shared turns in the same copy, Claude Code loads the copy's .claude skills, commands and agents and its plugin settings. A plugin those settings enable may bring hooks and MCP servers. An added folder's CLAUDE.md loads only when your own Claude Code setting turns that on. VIKI Agent's Bot rules tell the Bot to read the copy's top-level CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with its tools before it reads or changes files there, and to follow them for that work: an instruction to the model, not a check (Bot rules). The Bot's settings ask Claude Code to skip the vault's own instruction files (What a Bot reads).
  • Pushing
    a Bot's instructions can tell it not to push. That is a request to the model. VIKI Agent does not enforce it.
  • Hooks off for VIKI Agent's own Git
    its own Git commands in a Bot copy run with an empty private hooks folder, Commit and Integrate included, and so does the fast-forward Integrate makes of the copy's branch in the main folder. A restored copy is listed as no Bot's copy, and its own Git commands still run with hooks off.
  • Programs your Git settings name
    VIKI Agent's own Git commands in a Bot copy, the status bar's Git chip there included, also run without the filter drivers your Git config defines, start no signing program named by a relative path, and fetch no missing object. A Commit that such a program must sign is refused. Git LFS's own commands (git-lfs clean -- %f, git-lfs smudge -- %f, git-lfs filter-process and their --skip forms) still run, started from PATH, and are told to download nothing. Removing a copy and restoring an archived one run the same way. In every code folder, VIKI Agent's own Git ignores log.showSignature.

Git settings baseline. The folder's first Bot copy saves a fingerprint of the repository's local Git settings: its config and per-worktree config, the files they include, the hooks folder (.git/hooks and any core.hooksPath), info/attributes and core.attributesFile. Your global and system Git config are not part of it. Before VIKI Agent runs its own Git on that folder or one of its worktrees, it reads the settings again and compares: Commit, Integrate, Push, checkout, creating, removing, archiving and restoring worktrees, the Code view's changes and status, the status bar's Git chip, Decision's looks at code and saved checks. A difference stops the action with "This folder's Git settings or hooks changed after a Bot copy was made". The chip then runs no Git in that folder and shows status unknown with no branch, commit or change count, while that folder is the active workspace. The check does not apply to a folder that never had a Bot copy, or to a vault. Confirm the current settings in the Worktrees tab, which shows it as soon as it opens, saves what is there now as the new baseline, if the baseline is still the one you reviewed. Background work, such as the cleanup sweep and a copy's release, skips the folder until you confirm; Decision's looks and saved-check snapshots then read it as unknown.

Git reads in a vault. In a vault, at any policy, VIKI Agent's own Git reads (the status bar's Git chip and a note's history), and the identity read when a folder is registered or inspected, start none of the programs the folder's repository settings name: no fsmonitor hook, no filter driver (Git LFS's included), no signature program and no network transport. A missing object fetches nothing and no pack is written. The chip's status does not enter submodules. A folder holding HEAD, objects/ and refs/ but no .git is not a repository to these reads, and the trust step lists Git as present for it. Claude Code's own Git, in a chat started in that vault, still follows the vault's settings.

The saved baseline is deleted only when the folder is removed from the list, so the check continues after the folder's last copy is gone.

Any change to those settings trips the check, so ordinary commands do it too, whether you or Claude Code in the copy runs them: git push -u, switching to a branch that sets upstream tracking, adding or changing a remote, or git config for any repository setting. That is expected. The check cannot tell a harmless change from a hostile one, so confirming means you have looked at the current settings and accept them as the new baseline. Git LFS trips it too the first time Git runs it in a repository that never used it: it writes lfs.repositoryformatversion to the repository's config.

One exception: registering, refreshing or confirming it is the same folder before a change reads its identity with two Git commands (the root commit and the common Git directory) without the check. They read neither the index nor the working tree, and ran none of the repository-configured programs in testing.

VIKI Agent refuses a baseline instead of guessing when it cannot read the settings safely: a file over its limits (256 files, 4 MiB), a link, a home-relative or drive-relative path, a condition other than onbranch and hasconfig:remote.*.url in an includeIf, a settings file that changed while it was read, or a hooks folder that holds a subfolder or a hard-linked file (the layout of husky 5 to 8). When a Bot's first message hits this, the chat says "VIKI Agent can't read this folder's Git settings safely." and makes no copy.

Limits:

  • Hooks or filters replaced after a check are used by the rest of that operation. One check covers every Git command of one review, file view, search or saved-check snapshot, and of the reads before a Commit or Push. Commit, Integrate and Push check again once they hold the folder for writing. A Bot copy's own .git file is read again before each command in it, and a change is checked before that command runs.
  • VIKI Agent refuses Commit on a copy, and removing it, while a chat is running in it. It does not hold back Integrate or its other actions in the main folder meanwhile.
  • A repository config with submodule.recurse=true can send VIKI Agent's own Git commands other than status and diff into nested repositories in a copy. Their config and filters are outside the baseline. Every status and diff VIKI Agent runs in a copy carries --ignore-submodules, so those start no Git inside a nested repository. The status bar's Git chip does not carry it for a copy that is registered as a code folder of its own and is the active workspace. Cleanup keeps a copy whose index holds a nested repository's entry, one staged for deletion included, and its archive step refuses such an index rather than run git add -A on it.
  • Where a filter driver other than Git LFS's has a smudge or process command, cleanup keeps a released copy that has changes or commits found nowhere else; with a clean command only, it keeps one whose changed or new files are under that driver. A new copy in such a folder can list unchanged files as changed until a Git command you run in the copy refreshes its index.
  • Restoring an archived copy brings a Git LFS file back as its pointer file when the repository's own LFS store does not hold its object.
  • Push and its remote check, in a copy you registered as a code folder of its own, keep the remote's settings. A program those name by a relative path, such as remote.<name>.uploadpack, is a file in the copy.
  • More than 32 switched-off filter drivers and custom-named transports together, or one whose name holds = or is not UTF-8, makes Git unavailable in that folder's Bot copies.
  • A release it could not finish stays pending and is tried again at the next cleanup pass or deletion.

06Decision model

Decision can ask TypeSafe's model whether to tell you about something now or hold it. See Using VIKI Agent to turn it on and save a key.

What a Decision request carries

Before a request is sent, VIKI Agent:

  • strips every digit from facts, times and counts;
  • cuts excerpts to your chosen send level: titles only, or up to 200 or 2,000 characters, each ending "…" when cut;
  • drops any evidence under a folder or tag on your Never send list, counting what it drops.

Text from outside the vault travels only in its own part of the request.

What a request carries about an item is capped at 12,000 bytes. Past that:

  1. The least similar past items are dropped first.
  2. Then excerpts are cut further.
  3. Then the request is blocked rather than sent.

Every request also opens with a fixed guide on how to answer and carries the fixed questions. Neither holds anything about your items, and together they ride along on top of that cap, about 5.5 KB more.

How VIKI calls TypeSafe

The app makes only one call to TypeSafe, at https://api.typesafe.ai: asking a question.

  • Connection
    the call goes over TLS, with no redirects or system proxy. Any set cookie is ignored rather than refused.
  • Your key
    it rides only that one request's Authorization header, and nothing here logs it. It is sealed at rest (Windows: current-user DPAPI; macOS: the login Keychain; Linux: the Secret Service).
  • Rate
    VIKI keeps at most 2 requests in flight and sends at most 10 a minute.
  • Daily spend
    VIKI stops asking once the day's spend would reach the cap you set.
  • Retries
    a refused or failed request is not retried.
  • Call records
    the app keeps a sealed copy of what it sent and received for your last 20 calls. Context & loadout's Decision tab can show and copy it.

Version comparisons and proposed wording

With Compare with another model version on, a fresh decision's same request state is sent a second time, to that other version.

  • Limits
    it is sent under the same in-flight, per-minute, cooldown and daily-spend limits as the first.
  • Retries and records
    it is not retried, and it keeps no call record of its own.
  • Effect on live requests
    a rejected key or a busy reply to it pauses or cools the live requests too, as any request's reply would.

What VIKI learns from your answers is a handful of numbers that shift how loud and when, not your limits. It lives only in the app's own local database. Reset what VIKI learned and Delete all decision history both forget it.

Proposing new wording for one of Decision's questions is tried the same way. From your Propose this wording choice, each fresh decision also asks your proposed wording once.

  • Limits
    it is asked under the same in-flight, per-minute, cooldown and daily-spend limits as the comparison above, and it counts toward the same cap.
  • Retries and records
    it is never retried, and it keeps no call record of its own.
  • Effect on live requests
    a rejected key or a busy reply to it pauses or cools the live requests too.
  • Storage
    the wording itself is sealed at rest the same way your key is, in the app's own local database.
  • What reaches TypeSafe
    the wording, in its trial requests while it is tried and, once you approve it, in every request.
  • Approving or rejecting
    doing so in Approvals is the only thing that changes which wording new decisions ask.

A proposed wording is refused if it contains any of these:

  • control characters;
  • line or paragraph separators;
  • private-use or unassigned characters;
  • characters a screen would draw as nothing at all, such as zero-width ones.

An ordinary space is fine.

Vault upkeep proposals

With Self-improvement also proposing vault upkeep, three more candidate kinds land straight in Approvals rather than a chat draft:

  • linking two notes;
  • marking an older note as replaced;
  • archiving a project's ticked tasks.

What a proposed pair sends follows the rules above:

  • Paths
    each note's path in the vault.
  • Excerpts
    an excerpt, cut to your chosen send level: the line that mentions the other note, or the note's opening.
  • Held-back notes
    anything under a Never send folder or tag (written in its frontmatter or anywhere in the note) is held back. Here, a held-back note on either side blocks the whole pair, not just that one note.

A ticked-tasks proposal sends its tasks file's path and project name, never the tasks themselves.

Every request also carries the following, titles only, never a note's own text:

  • the titles of notes changed since yesterday;
  • the titles of items shown to you lately;
  • the items you most recently marked mute or wrong;
  • your recent feedback.

Never send applies to them the same way.

Approving or rejecting one of these proposals sends nothing about the change itself.

  • Approve
    only marks the row approved and hands you a drafted chat message for that one edit. Nothing in your vault changes until you send that yourself.
  • Feedback
    either act still counts as your feedback on that item: useful, or wrong for Reject. Later requests carry it under the item's fixed title, like any other feedback.

A proposal can never name a path this vault already protects:

  • AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, claude.local.md and the other instruction files at any depth, case or width;
  • hidden folders;
  • .git, .claude and the vault's other tool folders;
  • _raw/ at any depth;
  • at the vault's root, system/ (so system/memory/), _templates/ or 00-inbox/.

This is checked again each time: when VIKI first notices it, when it is filed, and again at every read-back or approval.

Skill suggestions

With Self-improvement also able to suggest one of your vault's own skills, VIKI reads that vault's skills. It matches them to the chat you have open by its title alone, entirely on this computer.

A request about the suggestion carries only fixed wording, its kind and its title, "A skill for this chat". So does every later request that mentions it once you have seen, used or dismissed it.

  • Skill details
    the skill's own name, its description and the skills the chat already used never reach TypeSafe.
  • Chat title
    the chat's title is sent only as the name of the chat you have open.
  • Use this skill
    only puts that skill's / command in the chat's own message box. Nothing is sent until you do.
  • Untitled chats
    an offer to make a skill from an untitled chat is titled "This chat", so the chat's first message is not sent as its title.

What VIKI starts or offers on its own

Look on my behalf

With Look on my behalf set to Allowed, the default, VIKI starts a plan-mode Claude Code chat in a trusted code folder on its own, without a click. Ask first only offers Take a look.

  • Message
    fixed text that names no folder, path, file or diff.
  • What it sends
    the chat reads the folder itself and sends what it reads to the selected model provider through Claude Code, as your chats there do.
  • Folder settings
    the folder's own instructions, hooks and settings, which you acknowledged when you trusted it, apply to a look as to any chat there.

Warning

The app checks those acknowledgements when you trust the folder and not again later. So hooks or MCP servers a later change adds, such as a pull, run in a look too.

Second looks and project plans

With Take a second look at my work and Plan next steps for my projects set to Allowed, the default, VIKI also starts their plan-mode chats in the vault on its own. Each waits for your approval before it changes anything.

  • What a second look reads
    only the first line of its own plan, to name the kind of finding. It keeps neither the plan nor your chat's text.
  • Your approval
    whether you approved that plan is kept with VIKI's record of that chat in the app's own local database, as the chat's mode is.
  • Stalled projects and overdue tasks
    a plan VIKI starts for these is read and kept the same way. Its message names one note in your vault and none of its text. VIKI picks no note that Never send holds back.

Message drafts

A message draft VIKI offers is fixed text it writes itself, with no note, web address or chat text in it. It goes into your message box only when you select it. It leaves this computer only when you send it, as any message you write.

Run my saved checks

With Run my saved checks set to Allowed, VIKI starts a trusted code folder's saved checks on its own when the folder moves to a new commit. That includes a commit a pull brought in. It runs them the same way Run in the Checks tab does. Ask first, the default, only offers Run checks.

  • What runs
    each check is a command you wrote, run with your account's rights.
  • No sandbox
    none is a sandbox, and a check can change files and use the network.
  • Check details
    VIKI reads no check's name, command or output.
  • Which checks
    VIKI runs only checks you have run in that folder before.

Suggest destinations for my inbox

With Suggest destinations for my inbox set to Allowed, the default, VIKI starts the inbox's suggestion run on its own. Ask first only offers Suggest destinations.

This is the run Ask VIKI to suggest starts:

  • Session
    a new Claude Code session with only Read, Glob and Grep and no MCP server, one reply, ended after five minutes.
  • Permissions
    the run denies any permission request it raises, as it does when you start it from the triage.
  • What it sends to Claude
    the name, the captured value and the first 600 characters of each capture in 00-inbox/, up to 100, and your project names.
  • Vault reads
    it can read files in your vault with those tools.
  • Suggestions
    it keeps them in memory until VIKI Agent closes. Nothing in your vault changes until you send the filing draft.
  • When none starts
    VIKI starts none while Never send holds a tag, a folder over a capture or a folder in 10-projects/.

07Optional messaging bridges

Mattermost and Slack or Discord each serve one configured human owner in a verified private direct message.

  • Conversation
    each bridge has its own conversation in Claude Code's auto permission mode and stays pinned to the startup workspace.
  • Approvals
    Claude Code's classifier, not the DM, approves most actions. Requests it still makes reach the DM as cards.
  • Manual mode
    where auto mode is unavailable, Claude Code starts the conversation in Manual mode instead, and every action reaches the DM as a card.
  • Mode chip
    if you open a bridge's conversation in the app, its mode chip can switch that conversation like any chat. After !viki new, the next conversation starts in auto again.

A bridge does not sandbox Claude Code or expand Claude Code's own permissions.

What leaves this computer

Trust the configured Mattermost server, or Slack or Discord, and the owner account before connecting.

  • All bridges
    prompts, final replies and complete permission or question requests leave this computer and follow the service's retention policy.
  • Mattermost progress
    on Mattermost, progress also leaves it while Claude works: the elapsed time, the step count, one fixed activity phrase and Claude's latest short note of up to 280 characters.
  • Activity phrase
    it comes from a fixed table. An MCP tool shows as "using a connected tool" and an unknown tool as "working". The phrase names no tool, file, path or command.
  • Progress note
    the note is Claude's own text, like a final reply, so it can mention files, paths or commands.

Warning

Service operators and anyone controlling the owner account are part of this trust boundary. Enable MFA and review retention before sending content. Local Reset and exports do not remove remote copies.

Once you send !viki questions on, a waiting question's header, text, options and descriptions from any other desktop chat also leave this computer in the same direct message.

  • Off by default
    this is off by default and only for the current connection, so it must be turned on again each time the bridge reconnects.
  • Who can answer
    anyone controlling the owner account can turn it on and answer those questions, the same way a desktop choice would, under that chat's own permission mode.
  • Permission cards
    desktop permission cards are not sent this way.
  • Stopping
    this stops when the bridge stops or you send !viki questions off.

Replying from the DM

A request from the bridge's own conversation can be answered three ways: with its command, with a plain message, or, on Mattermost only, with a reaction. Each request shows its !viki allow, !viki deny, !viki pick or !viki answer command.

Plain messages:

  • One request waiting
    when a request of the bridge's own conversation is the only request waiting as your message arrives (a relayed desktop question counts), a plain message answers it: allow or deny for a permission request, or option numbers or your own words for a question.
  • Several requests waiting
    while such a request waits beside another request (a relayed desktop question counts), nothing is sent to Claude and the reply points to the commands.
  • Other text
    other text on a permission request gets a hint and is not sent.
  • A running turn
    while a turn of the bridge's conversation runs and none of its own requests is waiting, a plain message is added to that turn.

Reactions, on Mattermost only:

  • Thumbs-up and thumbs-down
    a thumbs-up (+1, thumbsup) allows once and a thumbs-down (-1, thumbsdown) denies, from the owner account, in the bot's direct message, on the request's detail or instructions post, once the request has been fully posted.
  • Confirmation
    the WebSocket frame is only a candidate. It counts only after VIKI Agent reads the post's reactions from Mattermost and finds a matching owner reaction in that channel.
  • Questions
    questions and relayed desktop questions take no reactions.

Allow once still needs the complete request, and each request is answered once. Such a request has no time limit: it ends when you answer it, send !viki stop or !viki new, or the bot stops.

Every turn of the bridge's conversation is posted while it is active, including a turn Claude Code starts by itself, such as a background agent's report. After !viki stop or !viki new, such a turn is not posted and its requests are denied until your next message.

Setting up a bridge

Set up each provider in Messaging:

  1. Select Set up on its card.
  2. Fill in its fields.
  3. Select Save changes.

Saving seals the entered tokens in the app database (Windows: current-user DPAPI; macOS: the login Keychain; Linux: the Secret Service). It also stops any bridge running with the previous settings. Saved settings apply without restart.

  • Connecting
    turn a provider's bot on with its switch to connect.
  • Leaving a bot on
    it reconnects on its own the next time VIKI Agent starts in the workspace it was turned on in. It stays off in any other workspace until you turn it on there.
  • Reconnecting on its own
    a bot that reconnects this way is reachable again as soon as VIKI Agent starts, before you have looked at the desktop. Its ready DM is the visible signal, and every tool approval still needs your answer to a current request.

Status and tokens:

  • Refresh status
    reads state without enabling or reconnecting.
  • Status
    shows only fixed state names, fixed stop reasons and on/off flags, without tokens, account IDs, server URLs or message text.
  • Settings card
    shows each provider's saved non-secret values (such as the Server URL or a member or user ID), and never a token.
  • Launch token
    the local launch token is separate from provider bot and app tokens and is not sent to the providers.

Network connections and limits

These bridges make outbound HTTPS and WSS connections. The local listener remains on loopback.

  • Mattermost
    uses the configured HTTPS base and a closed set of API paths, including reading a post's reactions.
  • Slack
    uses its fixed API host and a validated Slack Socket Mode URL.
  • Discord
    uses its fixed v10 API and Gateway. Discord's configured client URL identifies the app in its HTTP User-Agent header and is not fetched.
  • All clients
    TLS verification is enabled. The clients refuse redirects, cookies, compressed HTTP responses and malformed JSON. They do not use environment proxies or retry a failed post.

On Mattermost, reactions, typing and post edits go through a separate progress client with its own connection. It allows nothing before it is bound. Afterwards it allows only:

  • the reactions 👀, ✅, ⚠️ and ⏹️ as the bot user;
  • removing the bot's own 👀;
  • typing and posts in the bound direct message;
  • edits to posts that client created.

Its failures stay local. A rate limit starts its own cooldown, and a failed call ends progress for that turn, without stopping the bridge or answering a request.

Size limits:

ItemLimit
HTTP request and raw response bodies128 KiB, within a five-second request deadline
WebSocket frames128 KiB
Rendered Mattermost posts12 KiB of UTF-8
Slack posts4000 characters
Discord posts2000 UTF-16 units
An individual messageCan expand to at most 32 posts
Each bridge's queueAt most 32 queued posts and 384 KiB
Assistant responses64 KiB of source text and four Mattermost-format posts of 12 KiB each
Mattermost Bot result notices8 KiB after chat formatting

Assistant responses may be shortened with a direction to check the desktop. An incomplete or oversized permission request offers Deny only; Allow once requires the complete request to have reached the DM.

How a post looks depends on your server or workspace and your mobile app. VIKI Agent hasn't been checked against every version.

Stopping and reconnecting

Each of these stops that bridge from accepting approvals straight away, before its connection finishes closing:

  • turning a bot off;
  • saving or removing its settings;
  • a connection failure it cannot recover from.

When a bridge stops:

  • Pending requests
    pending requests in that bridge are denied. The other providers and desktop conversations remain separate.
  • Stop notice
    a bot that had posted its ready message then posts one fixed line naming the reason when the service is reachable. It waits at most 3 seconds for it.
  • Stop reasons
    Messaging shows the reason, such as a rejected token, an unreachable service, a safety limit, a conversation error, a changed request or an unexpected error.

Warning

Stopping cannot undo an Allow already delivered locally or retract a post already sent. Check the DM and desktop after an uncertain receipt; choices and posts are not automatically retried.

After a stopped connection, turn that provider's bot on again once cleanup and its cooldown allow it. Slack connection renewal and Discord reconnect requests also require this manual step.

  • Reconnecting
    retains rate limits and waits for fresh messages, without replaying offline commands.
  • Restart
    a restart is needed if the startup workspace changed or the bridge could not shut down cleanly.
  • Across launches
    saved settings and the on/off choice persist across launches, subject to the reconnect rule above.

08Optional Voicebox voice

Read aloud and hands-free can speak through Voicebox, a separate program you install and run on this computer. See Using VIKI Agent for setup.

VIKI Agent sends the text of a reply to whatever answers at the configured Voicebox address. That address must be http on 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1].

Warning

Voicebox has no authentication. Any program listening at that address receives the text sent to it and can present itself as ready and offer its own voices. Set the address only to a Voicebox you trust.

  • Calls
    the app server makes only three calls there: a status check, a GPU check and one request to synthesize speech.
  • Redirects
    it follows no redirect.
  • Answers
    it caps every answer (256 KiB of JSON, 8 MiB of audio) and accepts only a well-formed WAV.
  • The app's own voice requests
    they need the same launch token as its other private requests and are marked not to be cached. They answer a failure with a fixed code rather than error text, and log only that fixed code, with no text.
  • Hands-free reports
    a hands-free report carries only a fixed event and code, and only those two values are logged.

Voicebox is a separate program: once it has the text, how it handles it is its own.

09Optional natural voices

Natural voices are VIKI's own copy of Voicebox 0.5.0's CUDA server and two models, Qwen3-TTS 0.6B CustomVoice and Kokoro-82M. See Using VIKI Agent for setup and Known issues for the hardware it needs.

  • Installing
    they are installed only when you select Install natural voices in Settings › Chat on a supported Windows PC with an NVIDIA graphics card. A pack without Kokoro gets it from Add the fast voice.
  • Downloads
    VIKI downloads two pinned GitHub release files and 56 pinned Hugging Face files at two pinned model revisions (13 for Qwen3-TTS, 43 for Kokoro-82M).
  • Checks
    each file is checked against a pinned size and SHA-256 before use. Downloads go over https, with redirects followed only to https.
  • Storage
    VIKI unpacks the archives into a private folder in VIKI's own app storage.
  • Signing
    these binaries are not signed by VIKI or their publisher. Trust rests on the pinned hashes matching what is fetched.
  • Removing
    Remove in Settings deletes the installed files and what they downloaded. Installing again re-downloads them.

Once installed, VIKI starts its own Voicebox server, on a random loopback port, only when a reply needs a natural voice or you preview one in Settings.

  • Lifetime
    the server ends when VIKI closes and is stopped again after 5 minutes unused. While hands-free is on, the server stays ready to answer.
  • Offline
    it runs offline.
  • Previews
    a preview sends only a fixed sample sentence the way a reply does.
  • Audio
    Voicebox 0.5.0 documents its speech endpoint as streaming audio back without saving it to disk, and VIKI does not save it either.

Warning

Like your own Voicebox app above, the server has no authentication of its own. Any program on this computer that finds its port could ask it to speak.

Voicebox 0.5.0 also checks neither a caller's identity nor its Host header. So a web page open in a browser here could reach it too, through DNS rebinding or a plain cross-site form post. A browser's own local-network protections may block that.

10Bots and routine results

A Bot is built from an agent profile and has its own reopenable Claude Code conversation.

  • Bot conversation
    it keeps the profile revision and model it was prepared with.
  • Routine runs
    each routine run uses a fresh chat with the current profile.
  • Reading
    reading Bots or opening a Bot's conversation sends no message.

Bot memory

In every vault, new Bot chats and routine runs request a per-Bot directory for Claude Code auto memory: bot-memory/<bot UUID>/ in an ordinary vault, otherwise <data>/bot-memory/<workspace id>/<bot id>/ in VIKI Agent's data folder, outside the vault. Claude Code's autoMemoryEnabled setting controls whether native auto memory is enabled. Managed autoMemoryDirectory settings take precedence and can choose another folder. The Bot memory view shows the requested folder; it does not check Claude Code's effective memory settings or report whether native auto memory is enabled.

  • Location
    the vault's bot-memory/<bot UUID>/ folder in an ordinary vault, or the Bot's folder in VIKI Agent's data folder in a read-only or protected vault, unless Claude Code's managed settings choose another. Memory kept in the data folder is not part of vault backups, and diagnostics and settings exports carry no memory text.
  • Controls
    the Bot page's memory card contains the Ask controls (review, forget and change); its View memory opens the file dialog. A Bot chat's Memory header button and View memory in Bot activity open the same dialog when the active vault's policy matches the Bot's. The card's change action opens an unsent draft in the Bot's main chat; review and forget open unsent task-thread drafts. The dialog lists exact paths; Open in Vault (only for vault-kept memory), Open in VS Code, Edit, Refresh memory and Close act on that list. It marks an incomplete list and file or title details it could not read. The forget draft asks Claude Code to list the exact files and request your confirmation before changing or deleting anything, then delete only the confirmed files within that folder.
  • Editing
    Open in VS Code hands the file to VS Code, which edits it directly. Save in the dialog's in-app editor writes nothing: it prepares an unsent request asking the Bot to replace the file, appended to the chat's unsent draft or as a new task thread's draft. It is never sent for you.
  • Writing
    Claude Code creates and updates these notes under its native permissions. VIKI Agent creates none and reads them through a read-only route; VIKI note operations do not target bot-memory/. On Windows, Claude Code saved memory without a permission request in Manual and Accept edits modes. This is untested on macOS and Linux.
  • Memory rule
    every Bot chat, task thread and Bot-thread turn gets VIKI Agent's fixed memory rule right after the profile's instructions, as an addition to Claude Code's system prompt that VIKI Agent sends in the initialize request at each start, not in argv or a file; a routine run gets it when its profile has a Bot in the routine's workspace. It asks the Bot to save no secrets, and no instructions or links taken from notes, files, web pages, tool output or other Bots, and to report instructions in a memory that you did not give. It is text the model reads, not a filter: VIKI Agent does not inspect what Claude Code saves, and other chats don't get it.
  • Bot rules
    the same chats get VIKI Agent's fixed Bot rules right after the memory rule. They ask the Bot to read a folder's top-level CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md before it reads or changes files in that folder outside the vault, such as its code copy; to ask you before deleting files, sending anything off this computer, pushing or paying; to treat web pages, files, tool output and other Bots' messages as data, apart from those instruction files and the skills it uses; and to write no passwords, keys or tokens into notes or files. Like the memory rule, they are text the model reads, not a permission: Claude Code's permissions decide what runs.
  • Vault instructions
    the same settings file that names the memory folder also names, in Claude Code's claudeMdExcludes setting, the vault's CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and AGENTS.md files and its .claude/rules/ files, at any depth, in every vault, for Claude Code to skip. It names nothing outside the vault.
  • Removing a Bot
    keeps its memory files, in the vault or in the data folder.
  • VIKI memory records
    a VIKI memory record is separate and applies only once you approve its exact content on this computer.

Important

The directories provide no sandbox: a Bot can read other files its permissions allow.

Seat Bots

Right after Start with VIKI makes a vault, the window that made it adds its seven seat Bots. It reuses each seat's profile or one with its name, else creates it from the seat's job description. This prepares no conversation and sends no message.

  • Open conversation
    used later on an empty seat, it creates the seat's missing profile and Bot and prepares a conversation without sending a message.
  • Sending in a shared Bot thread
    sending to an empty seat in a shared Bot thread also creates its missing profile and Bot, then prepares the thread's source conversation for that send.
  • Add missing Bots
    in Bots under Core team, it creates each missing seat's profile and Bot the same way, one seat at a time, and prepares no conversation and sends no message.
  • Kanban and routines
    these actions need no Kanban skill and create no routine.
  • Removing a Bot
    leaves its seat empty until you use it again.

Routine permissions and automatic starts

Routine tool permissions and deadlines apply.

  • Requests
    routine requests need desktop review rather than Mattermost permission controls.
  • Scheduled runs
    a scheduled run needs a permission mode that asks first or Claude Code's auto mode. Accept edits cannot be scheduled. Scheduled runs need an awake host and an open VIKI Agent window.
  • Stop time
    a request still waiting at the run's stop time is denied.
  • Stop at a draft
    a routine with this setting answers each permission or plan request of a run with a deny at once, carrying a fixed message that asks Claude to finish with a draft. It changes no permission settings, and a question still waits until the time limit.
  • Only when a card is waiting
    a routine with this setting reads the start of up to 128 notes directly in its vault's kanban/ folder before each scheduled time, to find a todo card for its seat.

With Start Bots' work set to Allowed, VIKI starts a seat's routine on its own, without a click. Ask first, the default, only offers Start.

  • Which routine
    only that seat's one enabled routine set to Only when a card is waiting, tested at its current version, in a vault whose policy is Ordinary.
  • Checks
    the run passes the checks a scheduled run passes, so its permission mode asks first or is Claude Code's auto mode.
  • Settings kept
    it keeps its routine's prompt, time limit and confirmation setting.

Mattermost result notices

Mattermost result delivery is off at each launch; you turn it on for each Bot. It is available only through the connected bridge's verified private direct message and for the same startup workspace.

  • Rechecks
    before a notice is sent, the queued notice rechecks the Bot, the workspace, the destination, your opt-in and the current attention policy.
  • Cancelled notices
    disabling delivery, removing or resetting the Bot, or closing the last VIKI Agent window cancels notices not yet sent. Turning delivery off and on does not revive an earlier notice.
  • Sent posts
    a post already sent cannot be retracted. An uncertain receipt is Unknown and is not retried automatically.
  • Local outcome
    the local routine outcome remains separate.

What a notice carries:

  • Reply text
    only runs from a Bot with delivery on collect their final reply text, and only in memory.
  • Successful runs
    a successful run can send up to 8 KiB of chat-formatted text, including the name, outcome, run ID, and shortening notice.
  • Failed, blocked, or expired runs
    eligible ones send fixed status text without partial replies.
  • Left out
    thinking, tool output, permission cards, and questions are not part of a notice.
  • Replies
    replies to these notices continue the dedicated Messaging conversation, rather than the Bot conversation or run chat.

How Decision applies:

  • Decision's rules
    they apply to the completed run, using that run's workspace mute and Later settings. This decision does not start another model run.
  • Held notices
    they remain local. Later expiry does not replay them.
  • Notice records
    Bot notice records are kept apart from Decision's own items and totals.

Bot records and removal

VIKI Agent's records of Bots and notice delivery store links, revisions, hashes, timestamps, and fixed attention or delivery states.

  • Not held
    they hold no instructions, prompts, reply text, credentials or Mattermost settings. They also do not record whether delivery is on, which starts off at each launch.
  • Profile instructions and chat drafts
    these are stored where they are for any profile or chat.

Remove Bot and Reset Bots in this workspace remove Bot links and delivery records and pause the Bot's enabled routines.

  • Kept locally
    profiles, conversations, routine history, and running attempts stay available locally.
  • Not removed
    backups you have already made and copies in Mattermost.

11Vault and app storage

In a vault whose policy is Ordinary, VIKI Agent can save notes itself on Windows, macOS and Linux. This includes the note actions, answering a Kanban card under Needs you, and keeping a chat image in the vault.

  • Conflicts
    a save stops if the note changed elsewhere first, and your draft stays.
  • Refused notes
    a read-only, locked or another user's note is refused.
  • Drives
    saving also needs a supported drive: NTFS on Windows, APFS on macOS, or ext4, XFS, Btrfs or tmpfs on Linux. Another drive, such as a network drive, keeps the vault read-only.
  • Replacing a note
    a replace keeps the note's permissions and, where the account allows it, its group, else drops group access. It does not keep extended attributes, Finder tags, ACLs or the creation date.
  • Instruction files
    in an Ordinary vault, Save on the Settings Instructions and Persona page replaces the vault's own top-level AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md with your edit. It replaces only an existing file with exactly that name, with the same conflict, permission and drive checks as a note save, and keeps its encoding, byte-order mark and line endings. It doesn't create, rename, move or delete either file, or save one in a subfolder, a protected vault or a code folder, and it doesn't go through Claude Code's permission prompts or hooks. It refuses text that a protected vault's file of the same name holds, because saving it would stop VIKI Agent from writing to this vault. While the vault is busy, for example during a backup, a save waits up to 10 seconds and then stops with nothing written. VIKI Agent keeps no previous version. During a save the file is briefly absent. If the save stops there (VIKI Agent stops, or the last step fails), the file stays absent until VIKI Agent next starts. That start finishes the save, unless something changed in the meantime (for example the vault moved, its policy changed, or another program wrote the file): then the save waits under Saves stopped partway through, with both texts kept in the vault's .viki- files. Discarding that record does not bring the file back; if another program wrote it, that version stays.
  • Saves at the same moment, off Windows
    off Windows, a file cannot be locked against other programs, so the app checks each step before and after it runs. When another program saves the note at the same moment, that version is kept and your save stops as a conflict. A new note's save can wait in Recovery instead.
  • Programs holding the note open
    a program that keeps the note open for writing during a save can still lose its own later write. On Windows, the save is refused while another program holds the note open for writing. See Known issues.
  • Protected places
    VIKI Agent does not save to a protected vault or to Claude Code's own folders (~/.claude). Changes made by Claude Code tools follow Claude Code's own permissions.
  • Backup restore
    a backup restore makes a new read-only vault folder.

Sealed app storage

Drafts, sent text and card answers kept by VIKI Agent are sealed in local storage:

  • Windows
    uses current-user DPAPI.
  • macOS and Linux
    use a key from the platform keychain for AES-256-GCM.

Sealing protects those stored values from casual inspection of the database.

Important

Sealing does not hide a conversation from Claude Code or the provider, and it does not anonymize every attachment or transcript. A process running as the same account has broader access than the app's browser-facing checks can prevent.

The local server and links

The local server uses a fresh launch token for private app requests. The token lasts for that launch.

  • Request checks
    the server checks the request's host and, for relevant requests, origin.
  • Your window and account
    treat an app window and your user account as private.
  • Reply Markdown
    it is displayed without raw HTML.
  • Links
    external links use the operating system's opener for HTTP, HTTPS or mail links. Opening a link can contact a remote site.
  • MCP server requests
    turning an MCP server on or off, or reconnecting it, can name only a server that chat's Claude Code already lists. The answer is a fixed status or error code rather than Claude Code's own error text, and VIKI Agent logs nothing for these requests.

12VIKI Agent's own window

VIKI Agent's own window is the Electron app in desktop/. It runs the server and shows its windows in Electron's own Chromium, with no Edge, Chrome or Chromium needed.

  • Launch token
    the server sends each window's address, launch token included, only over the pipe between the two programs. No command line holds it.
  • Request checks
    the same host, origin, content security policy and token checks apply as in a browser window.

These windows have context isolation, the renderer sandbox, no Node.js in the page or its workers, and no embedded web views, except the Magpie dashboard, which opens in its own isolated view (see Magpie routing and management).

  • Navigation
    apart from that dashboard, they load only VIKI Agent's own page, refuse navigation elsewhere, and open no new window. Links open in your default browser.
  • Granted only to VIKI Agent's own page
    the microphone (audio only), notifications and clipboard writes.
  • Refused
    camera, location, screen capture, clipboard reading, HID, USB and serial devices and every other request.
  • System settings
    the operating system's own microphone and notification settings still apply.
  • Spellcheck
    uses the macOS system spellchecker. It is off on Windows and Linux, so no dictionary is ever downloaded there.
  • Chromium's sandbox
    the window refuses to open at all, showing an error dialog instead, when Chromium's sandbox is off (see Known issues).

Quitting and closing:

  • Quitting the app
    tells the server to stop at once. Should the server still be running 15 seconds later, quitting ends its whole process tree.
  • Closing the last window
    instead lets a running turn finish first, for up to five minutes.

Started from source, this window runs the unmodified Electron binary that npm installs in desktop/node_modules.

Installed builds

An installed build runs only its own bundled server. VIKI_SERVER (see Configuration) is a developer override that an installed app ignores.

An installed app:

  • cannot be run as plain Node;
  • ignores NODE_OPTIONS and debugger flags;
  • gives pages loaded from local files no extra privileges;
  • loads code only from its own packaged files;
  • encrypts its cookies.

On Windows and macOS, it also checks at startup that its packaged files have not been altered, and ends itself if they have. Linux has no such check. An installed build does not check for updates.

13Sharing diagnostics and backups

Export diagnostics and Export settings preview a JSON file and redact recognized paths, account names and token-shaped values. An export holds its validated destination while saving; replacing that folder's path cannot redirect the file into another folder.

  • Workspace folder paths
    these are hidden unless you select Folder paths.
  • Credentials
    both exports filter recognized credential fields, credential assignments and URLs containing login details, including in workspace names.
  • Log tail
    a shortened log tail drops its first captured line so a cut-off credential label does not leave its value behind.
  • App logs
    these record warnings and errors. They do not record prompt text or frame bodies. An empty log can be normal.

Warning

Redaction is a filter, not a guarantee that all sensitive context has been removed. Review the exported file before sharing it.

Backups and portable settings:

  • Vault backups
    a vault backup contains note content and is not encrypted. Put it in a location whose access you control.
  • Conversations
    settings and diagnostics exports do not back up conversations. Use a chat's own export tools for a conversation.
  • Portable settings
    portable settings export and import exclude Bots, profiles, routines, and saved messaging settings.
  • App database backups
    an app database backup includes Bot links, delivery metadata, sealed messaging settings, Bot usage counts and Decision data as it was when the backup was made. Deleting Decision data later in Data does not change the backup; Claude Code owns its conversation history separately.

See Sessions and data for retention and Reset consequences.

Rolling back after an upgrade

Each upgrade step of app.sqlite3 first makes a verified copy of the database as it was, app.sqlite3.v<N>-backup-<id>.sqlite3 beside it, where <N> is the version before that step. A build from before the step refuses the upgraded database. The step that added the Bot usage log, for example, is version 41, so it leaves app.sqlite3.v40-backup-<id>.sqlite3; restoring that copy drops any usage rows logged since.

For rollback:

  1. Close the app.
  2. Restore the copy whose version matches the older build, with that build and the same Windows account or macOS/Linux keychain item that sealed the values.

In the recipes below, <data> is the app-data folder: %LOCALAPPDATA%\viki-agent on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/viki-agent on macOS and $XDG_DATA_HOME/viki-agent (~/.local/share/viki-agent by default) on Linux. <backup> is the full path of the copy whose v<N> is the older build's version; if several match, use the newest. Each recipe moves the current database and any -journal, -wal and -shm files into a new folder next to <data> (private on macOS and Linux, where mkdir -m 700 makes it so), so nothing is deleted, then puts a copy of the backup in place. It stops if that folder already exists. To roll back again, first move or rename the earlier hold folder. Write an apostrophe in a path as '' in PowerShell and as '\'' in the shell. Run it with the app closed.

On Windows, in PowerShell:

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$hold = '<data>-rollback-hold'
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $hold) { throw "$hold already exists" }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $hold | Out-Null
foreach ($suffix in '', '-journal', '-wal', '-shm') {
    $file = "<data>\app.sqlite3$suffix"
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file) { Move-Item -LiteralPath $file -Destination $hold }
}
Copy-Item -LiteralPath '<backup>' -Destination '<data>\app.sqlite3'

On macOS and Linux, in a shell:

set -eu
data='<data>'
backup='<backup>'
hold="$data-rollback-hold"
mkdir -m 700 -- "$hold"
for suffix in '' -journal -wal -shm; do
    if [ -e "$data/app.sqlite3$suffix" ]; then mv -- "$data/app.sqlite3$suffix" "$hold/"; fi
done
cp -- "$backup" "$data/app.sqlite3"

Then start the older build with the same Windows account or keychain item. Copy no credential, keychain item or sealing-key-id record, and do not edit the database's user_version. The backup stays where it is, as does the hold folder.

Warning

After a rollback, everything stored after that upgrade is gone, such as settings saved after it. A rollback restores only app state as of the backup, not later changes or Claude Code's conversation history.

Changing the database's version in place is not a supported downgrade.
